---
title: "A small molecule for reperfusion injury"
description: >-
  Restoring blood flow to ischemic tissue causes injury of its own. We are
  developing small molecules against a metabolic enzyme to blunt it.
order: 40
toc: false
---

Restoring blood flow to ischemic tissue is necessary, and it is also injurious.
When oxygen returns to a tissue that has been without it, the abrupt resumption
of mitochondrial electron transport produces a burst of reactive oxygen species
that damages the tissue the intervention was meant to salvage. This is the
central problem of reperfusion injury, and it limits the benefit of
revascularization after myocardial infarction, of thrombectomy in stroke, and of
transplantation, where every organ is reperfused by definition. No approved
therapy addresses it directly.

Ischemia leaves a metabolic signature. Substrates accumulate during oxygen
deprivation and are consumed when oxygen returns, and the manner of their
disposal determines how much oxidative damage follows. Our work on the metabolic
response to low oxygen identified an enzymatic step that governs how tissue
handles one of these accumulated substrates on reperfusion, and that can be
inhibited pharmacologically to shift the balance away from injury.

We are developing small molecule inhibitors of that step. Work so far has covered
target validation and early compound discovery. Current effort is directed at
potency, selectivity, and the pharmacologic properties needed for testing in
animal models of ischemia and reperfusion.
